meta.title: Error Handling & Stream Recovery (F-3) — final plan
meta.basedOn: candidate-c (judge-selected winner) + grafts from candidate-b (HostCommand.KillServer / RestartAdbServerUseCase) and candidate-a (shared TIMEOUT_REASON_PREFIX constant), plus two late hardware measurements the winner and the judge did not have (idempotent warm start-server; WEDGED daemon).

goal: Make every discovery failure actionable and make an involuntary disconnect non-destructive, by (a) rendering F-2's four typed discovery outcomes through the already-shipped ErrorCard/CommandBlock/SourceListRow, (b) splitting the involuntary-disconnect path away from resumeLive's clear logic and giving it a FeedbackBar banner plus a Reconnect intent, and (c) removing the reproduced cold-adb-daemon livelock — and the second, distinct WEDGED-daemon failure mode found while measuring the fix — so the cards' recovery actions can actually succeed.
problemStatement: Three defects, none cosmetic. (1) F-2 deliberately left ToolMissing/NoDeviceFound/PollFailed unrendered: on a machine without adb, with nothing attached, or with adb failing mid-poll the user is shown the passive NO SIGNAL stage, which says nothing actionable. (2) F-4's merged code routes an involuntary USB disconnect into a state where the ONLY affordance offered is Resume Live (MirrorAnnotationStage.kt:292-298 renders it unconditionally whenever frozen != null), and resumeLive() clears the frozen bitmap and the staged annotation list — so a wiggled cable plus one click destroys unsent work, violating NFR-6. There is no reconnect path at all. (3) Reproduced on the attached Pixel 8 (38031FDJH00JVF): a cold adb daemon forks in 3.053 s against MirrorTuning.HostCommandTimeoutMs = 3_000L, so ProcessRunner's finally destroyForcibly()s adb mid-fork, the daemon never finishes starting, and the 2 s poll re-enters the same cold state forever — 41 consecutive timeouts, zero successes, recovering only when a human ran `adb devices -l` from a shell. Follow-up measurement showed the cold cost is a FIXED 3.03 s internal delay (identical on all three runs to the hundredth), so the 3000 ms budget missed by ~30 ms deterministically: never a flaky race, it fails on every attempt on a cold daemon, forever. A further measurement found a SECOND, distinct failure mode: a daemon that is alive but not serving (simulated with SIGSTOP) hangs `adb devices` indefinitely AND hangs `adb start-server` — so start-server is a 'make sure one exists' command, not a repair command, and only kill-server clears that state.
highLevelDescription: Three loosely-coupled changes in three layers that deliberately share no code path. DATA: HostCommand.StartServer and HostCommand.KillServer join the closed command set; AdbHostSource grows startServer() and killServer(); the POLICY lives in DeviceRepositoryImpl.observeDiscovery's loop as a BUDGETED ESCALATION — ListDevices at the existing 3 s HostCommandTimeoutMs, and only on a timeout-classified failure does the loop heal (StartServer under the new 15 s DaemonStartTimeoutMs; if StartServer itself times out the daemon is wedged rather than absent, so KillServer then StartServer; still failing surfaces PollFailed with the reason). The timeout classification is a shared TIMEOUT_REASON_PREFIX constant on DeviceCommandException referenced by its single producer (ProcessRunner.kt:79) and both consumers, so a reworded message cannot silently disarm the healing. PRESENTATION STATE: one new MirrorIntent.Reconnect with its own handler that touches neither currentFrozenFrame nor state.frozen; resumeLive() is left byte-for-byte unchanged so F-4's AC-51 survives; a derived MirrorUiState.canResumeLive stops the stage OFFERING the work-destroying affordance while disconnected; MirrorIntent.RetryDiscovery (plain re-poll) and MirrorIntent.RestartAdb (a real kill+start through RestartAdbServerUseCase, then a re-poll) are two distinct intents with two specified, tested handlers. PRESENTATION PROJECTION: two pure, Compose-free projections — MirrorUiState.errorCard(nowMs) -> MirrorErrorCard? and MirrorUiState.dropBanner() -> MirrorDropBanner? — are the assertable surface for every `test`-verified AC; a new stateless MirrorErrorStage renders the first through the shipped ErrorCard (+ SourceListRow rows), and the second is an existing FeedbackBar instance dropped into MirrorAnnotationStage's existing overlay Box. The winner's distinguishing structural choice is kept: NO new MirrorStage case. errorCard() is consulted only inside MirrorContent's existing MirrorStage.NoSignal branch, so an error card can never steal the stage from a frozen frame, a live mirror or the picker; F-2's shipped pure `stage` property is untouched and its tests cannot be destabilised. errorCard() returning null is what keeps AC-4's NoSignalStage on screen for the genuinely-no-error Detecting/Found cases.
background: F-1 (shell), F-2 (discovery/mirroring) and F-4 (drag-annotate-frozen-frame) are merged to development with 196 desktop tests green. ErrorCard, CommandBlock, SourceListRow (with F-2's `enabled` parameter), AppButton, StatusIndicator, DeviceChip and FeedbackBar all already exist in presentation-core-ui — FeedbackBar's own @Preview at FeedbackBar.kt:191-197 composes literally the FR-24 banner ('Stream dropped' / status Error / detail 'Annotations kept.' / actionLabel 'Reconnect' / actionVariant Primary), and ErrorCard's @Preview at ErrorCard.kt:158-165 composes literally comp 04. Design comps exist for AC-26 (04) and AC-27 (05) and do NOT exist for AC-28 or FR-24. This chain has already shipped one vacuous test (F-4's session-loss test, which passed against deleted code and was made non-vacuous by F-4's COR-1 fix), so every test below carries a named mutation. `.pipeline/sdd/docs/registry/*.json` does not exist in this repository (re-verified during this refinement pass: `.pipeline/sdd/docs/registry/` matches no files at all); the bug-registry recurrence check is therefore run against the real evidence this chain has — events.jsonl, inputs/reproduced-defect-adb-cold-start.md, inputs/CORRECTION-nfr-6-mechanism.md and the prior specs' recorded waivers — and recorded in knownRisksFromQA with a concrete watchFor and mitigation per entry.

AS-15: resumeLive() — the user-initiated Resume Live button, F-4's AC-51 — keeps clearing annotations and the frozen frame unchanged; only the involuntary onSessionLost path is rerouted away from it (binding decision 2 / FR-33).

AS-16: AC-28's device rows are individually clickable to mirror that device directly, with the primary button as a convenience shortcut to the top row, not a separate confirm step (binding decision 3 / FR-34).
AS-17: the banner's annotation count reads the same staged list F-4 already exposes (MirrorUiState.stagedCount / FrozenFrame.annotations) — no new counting logic.

AS-18 (new, candidate C): no new MirrorStage case is needed, because MirrorContent's existing NoSignal branch is reached exactly when the picker is closed, the platform is Android, nothing is frozen and no session is streaming — which is precisely the gate the error card needs.
AS-19 (new, candidate C): a MISSING adb is never cached by ToolResolver (it caches successes only), so a user-chosen path is picked up by the very next poll with no cache invalidation to write.

AS-20 (new, candidate C): `adb start-server` is idempotent and returns in ~10 ms against a warm daemon, so calling it before the first poll of every discovery collection costs nothing on a warm machine and the 15 s watchdog is never approached on the success path.

constraints.text: TEST INTEGRITY (hard): this chain shipped ONE VACUOUS TEST that passed against deleted code. Every test in testStrategy below names the exact line to break and the assertion that must then fail. AC-54's red run and T1's red run must be demonstrated against pre-fix/merged code and the output recorded in the spec directory before the fix lands.

TRACE-ID COLLISIONS, carried verbatim, renumber NOTHING: (1) SC-10/SC-11 collide with F-4's own SC-10 ('Escape dismisses, delete removes') and SC-11 ('Resume live after annotating'); (2) FR-23 collides with app-shell-window-layout's unrelated FR-23 ('signal colors render identically in light/dark'); (3) FR-24 collides with android-device-discovery-mirroring's unrelated FR-24 ('v1 screenshot-polling mirror transport'). All three are pre-existing. Stage 5 must treat these ids as spec-scoped, not globally unique.

commonTest names are plain camelCase only. A backtick name containing a comma, apostrophe or colon compiles on the JVM and fails compileTestKotlinIosArm64 with 'Name contains illegal characters' — this already broke the repo build once (F-1). A green desktopTest does not prove cross-target compilation.

withTimeoutOrNull only, never withTimeout, anywhere new — resultLauncher catches Throwable including CancellationException. The daemon-start path inherits this by routing through ProcessRunner, which already does it.

No literal Color(0x...), no raw .dp, no hardcoded TextStyle at any new call site. The two invented geometry values (banner alignment/padding) are named private constants in the file that uses them; DaemonStartTimeoutMs is a named MirrorTuning constant.

ProcessBuilder stays in exactly one file (data-device-impl desktopMain core/process/ProcessRunner.kt). start-server routes through ProcessRunner.run; no second spawn site, no spawnDetached. Audit: grep -rln "ProcessBuilder" --include="*.kt" . | grep -v /build/ must still print exactly one path.

No raw-argv or raw-String escape hatch on the device API. HostCommand gains a parameterless data object case and nothing else — StartServer carries no user input at all, so NFR-5's type-level guarantee is unchanged.

Every new user-facing string gets a referenced mirror_*-style key in presentation-core-localisation; grep each key for a call site before declaring done (F-4's T-12 precedent: no dead keys). Machine output — commands, serials, versions, diagnostics — carries no key at all, per presentation-core-ui/CLAUDE.md.
presentation-core-ui depends on presentation-core-styling only. Kit components take copy as parameters; MirrorErrorStage (in the feature module) resolves every label with stringResource.

The 196 pre-existing desktop tests stay green. Build per module — the Kotlin daemon is capped at 3 GB — then run the cross-target compile guard. A fresh worktree lacks local.properties; the orchestrator seeds it.

NFR-1 is out of scope but must not be contradicted: measured screencap mean 2665 ms / 0.4 fps on the Pixel 8. No step here assumes a higher frame rate, and MirrorTuning.CaptureFloorMs is left at 100L, unmeasured, with its harness note intact.

functional.text: Render ErrorCard instances for DiscoveryModel's typed discovery-failure states: ToolMissing (FR-23a / AC-26), NoDeviceFound (FR-23b / AC-27) and multiple-devices-connected (FR-23c / AC-28) — wiring only, zero new kit primitives. ID collides with app-shell-window-layout's unrelated FR-23; both are spec-scoped and neither is renumbered.

On a mid-session stream drop, show a non-blocking floating banner over the stale (frozen) mirror: 'Stream dropped' plus a kept-annotations detail line, primary action 'Reconnect'; staged annotations stay pinned and remain editable while disconnected. ID collides with android-device-discovery-mirroring's unrelated FR-24; both are spec-scoped and neither is renumbered.

Render DiscoveryModel.PollFailed as its own ErrorCard state, distinct from NoDeviceFound — title and body convey a tool-level failure ('adb itself failed') rather than an empty bench ('nothing attached'); the footer carries the tool name and the failure reason string; primary action 'Retry'. Binding decision 1.

Split F-4's session-termination handling into two distinct code paths: the involuntary disconnect (onSessionLost) must never reach resumeLive's clear-annotations / clear-frozen-frame logic, and the UI must stop offering Resume Live while the session is Lost (derived MirrorUiState.canResumeLive). The user-initiated Resume Live control (F-4's AC-51) keeps its clear-and-return-to-live behaviour unchanged. Binding decision 2.

The multiple-devices card's inline device list uses SourceListRow with every usable row enabled (F-2's `enabled` parameter) and clickable to mirror that device directly; an unusable (unauthorized) device still renders, disabled, per F-2's A11Y-6. The card's primary action is a convenience shortcut equivalent to clicking the top-listed row — not a separate flow, modal or confirm. Binding decision 3.

The banner's 'Reconnect' action re-attempts the capture session against the same sessionDeviceId carried by MirrorSession.Lost; on success the stage returns to live, the banner dismisses and all staged annotations remain intact; on repeated failure the banner persists rather than silently disappearing. No new retry/backoff machinery — a failed reconnect re-enters the existing observeFrames .catch { onSessionLost } path, which puts the state straight back into Lost.

MINTED HERE (binding decision 4). Cold-daemon livelock fix, as a BUDGETED ESCALATION rather than a pre-emptive call. Add HostCommand.StartServer AND HostCommand.KillServer to the closed deviceless set (adding cases is sanctioned by data-device-api/CLAUDE.md; a raw-argv escape hatch is not), expose AdbHostSource.startServer() / killServer(), and add MirrorTuning.DaemonStartTimeoutMs = 15_000L as a WATCHDOG (not a calibration constant - cold start is a fixed 3.03s, so 15s carries ~5x headroom). The ladder, owned by DeviceRepositoryImpl's poll loop so it is testable under virtual time with no hardware:
  1. ListDevices at its existing 3_000L HostCommandTimeoutMs. Success -> emit Found/NoDeviceFound, done.
  2. On a TIMEOUT-classified failure only (not a parse error, not a non-zero exit): StartServer under DaemonStartTimeoutMs. This covers the cold daemon, measured at a fixed 3.03s.
  3. If StartServer ITSELF times out, the daemon is wedged rather than absent: KillServer, then StartServer. This is the only sequence that recovers a wedged daemon, and it is the same mechanism AC-27's 'Restart adb' button invokes.
  4. Still failing -> emit PollFailed carrying the reason. Never loop silently.
DELIBERATE DEVIATION from preparation's 'before the first discovery poll and again after any timeout-failed poll'. The pre-first-poll call is WITHDRAWN on measured evidence: against a WEDGED daemon (alive but not serving) `adb start-server` HANGS, so an unconditional pre-poll call would burn the full 15s watchdog on every poll - a second livelock, five times worse than the 3s one being fixed. Cost of the ladder on a genuinely cold start is ~6s once (one 3s timeout + one 3.03s start), which is the price of not introducing that regression. Kept distinct from FR-32 (a rendering requirement) because this is behavioural, and conflating them would make an AC-53 waiver unreadable.

MINTED HERE. Every error card's recovery action performs real work rather than waiting out the 2s poll. TWO distinct intents, because copy must agree with behaviour (presentation-core-ui/CLAUDE.md):
  - MirrorIntent.RetryDiscovery restarts the discovery collection through a nonce the ViewModel's flatMapLatest gate already reads, re-emitting Detecting and polling immediately. AC-26's secondary 'Retry' and AC-53's primary 'Retry' map here.
  - MirrorIntent.RestartAdb runs RestartAdbServerUseCase (KillServer then StartServer, each budgeted) and then bumps the same nonce. AC-27's primary 'Restart adb' maps HERE, not to RetryDiscovery.
GRAFTED from candidate-b per the judge. A button labelled 'Restart adb' that only re-polls is the 'card that lies' the brainstorm warned about, and measurement makes it concrete: StartServer alone cannot clear a wedged daemon, so without KillServer the button would be unable to fix the very state a user presses it in.

nonFunctional.text: Stream-drop handling must preserve all staged annotations and the frozen frame without loss across a disconnect/reconnect cycle. CURRENTLY VIOLATED by merged F-4 code: the only affordance offered while Lost is Resume Live, whose handler clears both. FR-33 is the fix.
Device picker, annotation popovers and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers, Tab/Enter for error-card and banner actions).
All screens support full light and dark theme parity using the defined signal-color system (red = bug, green = fixed, orange = warning, blue = measurement) with sufficient contrast in both themes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given adb is not found on PATH (DiscoveryModel.ToolMissing), then an ErrorCard renders with the platform install command in a copyable CommandBlock, primary action 'Locate adb…', secondary action 'Retry', and a footer line listing the probed paths and $ANDROID_HOME state.

Given no Android device is detected after repeated polls (DiscoveryModel.NoDeviceFound), then an ErrorCard renders with the kill-server command, primary action 'Restart adb', secondary action 'Boot emulator instead', and a footer line showing tool version, last-poll age and attached count.

Given 3 devices are connected simultaneously, then an ErrorCard renders an inline SourceListRow list of all attached devices (not a modal), every usable row enabled and clickable to mirror that device directly (an unauthorized device still renders, disabled, per F-2's A11Y-6), with the card's primary action labeled 'Mirror <top device>' as a one-click shortcut to the first-listed device.

Given a stream drops mid-session with staged annotations present, then a non-blocking banner appears over the stale (frozen) mirror reading 'Stream dropped' plus a kept-annotations line, with a primary 'Reconnect' action; 'Resolve & Send' remains clickable and every staged annotation remains pinned and unchanged while disconnected.

Given adb itself fails or times out mid-poll (DiscoveryModel.PollFailed), then an ErrorCard renders distinct from the NoDeviceFound card — title and body convey a tool-level failure (not an empty device bench), the footer shows the tool name and failure reason, primary action 'Retry'.

Given staged annotations and a frozen frame exist, when the session is lost involuntarily (onSessionLost, not a user-initiated Resume Live click) and later reconnects, then every staged annotation and the frozen frame are bit-for-bit unchanged before and after the cycle; this test is run against the pre-fix code first and demonstrated to fail before the fix lands.
Given any ErrorCard instance (AC-26/27/28/53) or the stream-drop banner (AC-29), then every primary/secondary/copy/row action is reachable via Tab and activatable via Enter/Space without a pointer.

Given the light and dark themes, then ErrorCard (all four states) and the stream-drop banner meet the project's existing contrast baseline (same method as presentation-core-styling's PaletteContrastTest), with no state relying on a signal color that differs between themes.

architecture.approach: Three loosely-coupled fixes in three layers that share no code path, plus one deliberate routing choice that avoids touching F-2's shipped state machine. (1) DATA — HostCommand.StartServer joins the closed set; AdbHostSource.startServer() runs it through the single ProcessRunner under MirrorTuning.DaemonStartTimeoutMs; the policy of when to call it lives in DeviceRepositoryImpl.observeDiscovery's loop, keyed on an internal DeviceCommandException.isTimeout() matcher, so it is drivable under virtual time against a fake source. (2) PRESENTATION STATE — MirrorIntent.Reconnect reads MirrorSession.Lost.deviceId, sets sessionDeviceId and reduces session = Streaming, and touches neither currentFrozenFrame nor state.frozen; resumeLive() is untouched; MirrorUiState.canResumeLive = frozen != null && session !is Lost makes the footgun unavailable in the UI as well as the reducer; MirrorIntent.RetryDiscovery bumps a nonce the discovery gate already reads. (3) PRESENTATION PROJECTION — two pure functions in core/discovery/DiscoveryErrorProjection.kt map state to Compose-free value types (MirrorErrorCard, MirrorDropBanner); a new stateless MirrorErrorStage renders the first through the shipped ErrorCard + SourceListRow rows, and the second is a FeedbackBar instance in MirrorAnnotationStage's existing overlay Box. (4) ROUTING — errorCard() is consulted only inside MirrorContent's existing MirrorStage.NoSignal branch. No new MirrorStage case, no change to the shipped `stage` property.
architecture.rationale: Each choice is the smallest change that makes the bug class structurally unavailable rather than merely absent. Two intents in two functions is what stops 'deliberate discard' and 'involuntary loss' from ever being conflated again — conflating them is how the NFR-6 violation happened. The daemon watchdog is the only option where the new number bounds 'something is wrong' instead of guessing a per-machine duration: once the daemon is warm every later `devices -l` is 0.01 s, so the success path never depends on the budget being tight, which is exactly the property raising HostCommandTimeoutMs lacks. Keeping the policy in the repository loop (not the datasource) is what makes it hardware-free testable, and the loop is already the place that turns a failed poll into PollFailed. The pure-projection strategy is the only way the `test`-labelled ACs are genuinely assertable in a repo with no Compose UI-test harness, and it follows the module's own precedent (applyDiscovery, formatStatusLine, nextSelectableIndex are all separate pure files for this reason). Routing through the existing NoSignal branch rather than minting a MirrorStage case is candidate C's specific bet: it gives the 'never steal the stage from a frozen frame / a live mirror / the picker' guarantee for free from control flow instead of from a guard someone can delete, and it leaves F-2's `stage` property and tests literally unmodified.

alternativesConsidered.title: Raise MirrorTuning.HostCommandTimeoutMs past the measured cold start
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: 3.053 s was measured on ONE machine, so any constant is a guess that fails on a slower host. HostCommandTimeoutMs also covers every deviceless command, so raising it makes a genuinely broken adb slower to report. And destroyForcibly() still kills adb mid-fork whenever the guess is wrong, so the livelock is reintroduced rather than removed.

alternativesConsidered.title: Escalating per-attempt ListDevices budget (attempt n gets n x base)
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Still kills adb mid-fork on every early attempt, so it still destroys the previous attempt's progress; recovery only happens when a budget accidentally overshoots. Replaces one magic constant with a magic growth curve and de-guesses nothing.

alternativesConsidered.title: Stop destroyForcibly()-ing a timed-out child so the daemon finishes in the background
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Correctly identifies the mechanism — which is why the chosen fix works — but contradicts data-device-impl/CLAUDE.md's load-bearing orphan-reaping rule and the shutdown hook, and destroyForcibly() is also what closes the child's pipes to unblock a drain parked on a grandchild's write end. A leaked screencap per timed-out frame would be catastrophic at frame rate.

alternativesConsidered.title: ProcessRunner.spawnDetached(['adb','start-server']) and let the 2 s retry loop recover
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Genuinely lazier and would work, but produces no success/failure signal, so PollFailed's reason stays a bare timeout note and a permanently broken adb is indistinguishable from a slow one — which is the diagnosis AC-53's card exists to show. spawnDetached also deliberately skips reaping registration (it exists for emulators the user owns).

alternativesConsidered.title: Fold PollFailed into the NoDeviceFound card
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: DiscoveryModel.PollFailed's own KDoc explicitly separates 'we learned nothing' from 'the bench is empty'; collapsing them tells a user holding a connected phone that there is no device. ErrorCard supports a fourth branch at zero new-primitive cost. T6 is the permanent guard on this decision.

alternativesConsidered.title: Reroute onSessionLost by changing resumeLive to conditionally preserve state
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Puts the two user intents back in one function, which is the exact shape that produced the NFR-6 violation, and risks F-4's confirmed AC-51. Two intents, two handlers, two tests instead.

alternativesConsidered.title: Add a MirrorStage.Error case and route the card from the pure `stage` property
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Candidate C's rejected alternative. It mutates F-2's shipped, separately-tested `stage` property and its ordering invariants (frozen-before-Streaming), and then needs its own guard to stop an error card stealing the stage from a frozen frame. Routing inside the existing NoSignal branch gets the same behaviour from control flow, with a zero-line diff to `stage`.

alternativesConsidered.title: Introduce a Compose UI-test harness (runComposeUiTest / ui-test-junit4) so AC-55 is asserted
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: New dependency plus catalog entries plus desktop test-source wiring, a real risk to the 196-green constraint, inside a spec whose framing is 'assemble, don't author'. Desktop focus-traversal assertions in an overlay Box are their own project. Deferred to its own spec; AC-55 is recorded as inspection, explicitly, not satisfied by a weak test.

alternativesConsidered.title: 'Locate adb…' as an inline path field built from the existing Input atom instead of a native dialog
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: The expensive half (persist the override, teach the resolver to probe it) is identical, so this saves about ten desktopMain lines while shipping a worse affordance than the comp specifies — 'Locate adb…' plainly means a chooser. FileDialog is the native platform feature and needs no new dependency.

alternativesConsidered.title: Widen AdbHostSource.probe() with a nullable userPath parameter instead of a new module edge
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Mutates a closed datasource contract for a UI feature and threads one nullable through three layers. ToolResolver already has three constructor seams of exactly this shape; a fourth plus one api-only Gradle edge is the smaller, more local change.

alternativesConsidered.title: Add HostCommand.KillServer so AC-27's 'Restart adb' literally restarts the daemon
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: Widens the closed set on a guess about what users need. The comp's own design already hands the user a copyable `adb kill-server && adb devices`; the button maps to start-server plus an immediate re-poll. The semantic gap is recorded in openQuestions with KillServer named as the upgrade path if hardware testing shows the re-poll is insufficient.

alternativesConsidered.title: Make the banner also cover a drop that happens while live (nothing frozen)
alternativesConsidered.whyRejected: AC-29 is explicitly about the stale frozen frame, nothing stale exists to float over while live (observeFrames nulls currentFrame when sessionDeviceId goes null), and today's NoSignal stage plus the already-wired StatusIndicatorState.Dropped covers that case. Pinning the last live frame would need a MirrorStage.Dropped or a reuse of Frozen and would reintroduce exactly the state conflation FR-33 removes.

components.name: DeviceCommandException.isTimeout()
components.responsibility: New internal file data-repository-impl/src/commonMain/kotlin/data/repository/impl/core/discovery/TimeoutMatcher.kt: `internal fun DeviceCommandException.isTimeout(): Boolean = exitCode == null && stderrTail.startsWith("timed out after")`. components.name: DeviceRepositoryImpl daemon-start policy
components.responsibility: Edit to the existing observeDiscovery loop (data-repository-impl/.../source/DeviceRepositoryImpl.kt:72-105). Order matters: the probe()-not-found short-circuit inside poll() still wins, so a genuinely absent adb reports ToolMissing and no start-server is attempted.

interfaces.name: AdbHostSource.startServer
interfaces.contract: public suspend fun startServer() — runs `adb start-server` under MirrorTuning.DaemonStartTimeoutMs. Idempotent and ~10 ms against a warm daemon. Throws DeviceCommandException on failure or watchdog expiry; callers in the poll loop convert that into DiscoveryModel.PollFailed and never let it escape observeDiscovery.

interfaces.name: buildHostArgv(toolPath, HostCommand.StartServer)
interfaces.contract: Returns exactly listOf(toolPath, "start-server"). No -H, no -P, no -s. Single construction point unchanged.

interfaces.name: DeviceCommandException.isTimeout
interfaces.contract: internal fun DeviceCommandException.isTimeout(): Boolean — true only for ProcessRunner's watchdog message shape (exitCode == null && stderrTail.startsWith("timed out after")). False for a non-zero exit, for a parse failure and for the IOException 'could not start' case. One behaviour, one call site, two tests.

interfaces.name: MirrorUiState.errorCard
interfaces.contract: internal fun MirrorUiState.errorCard(nowMs: Long): MirrorErrorCard? — pure. null when isPickerOpen, when session is Streaming, when frozen != null, when discovery is Detecting, and when Found yields fewer than two usable physical devices. ToolMissing/NoDeviceFound/PollFailed map one-to-one; Found with >1 usable physical device maps to MultipleDevices.

interfaces.name: MirrorUiState.canResumeLive

interfaces: DeviceCommandException.TIMEOUT_REASON_PREFIX (const "timed out after ") + DeviceCommandException.isTimeout(): the ONE shared classifier, referenced by its single producer (ProcessRunner.kt:79, which formats the reason) and its single consumer (DeviceRepositoryImpl's escalation ladder). lateEvidenceFolded: MEASURED: `adb start-server` against a HEALTHY warm daemon costs 0.00 s, leaves the daemon pid unchanged (78433 before and after — not restarted) and leaves `adb devices` reporting 38031FDJH00JVF. The healing step therefore costs nothing and bounces nothing on the common warm path.

MEASURED: cold `adb start-server` is 3.03 s on all three runs, identical to the hundredth — a FIXED internal delay in adb's fork-server path, not variable work. Consequences folded in: the old 3000 ms budget missed by ~30 ms DETERMINISTICALLY (never a flaky race — it fails on every attempt on a cold daemon, forever, which is why the symptom is a livelock rather than intermittent slowness); the 15 s DaemonStartTimeoutMs watchdog has ~5x headroom and stays a watchdog rather than a per-machine calibration; and the regression path is reproducible ON DEMAND with `adb kill-server` and needs NO timing tolerance in any test.

MEASURED and DECISIVE: a WEDGED daemon (alive but not serving, simulated by SIGSTOP on the daemon pid) hangs `adb devices` (>8 s, never returned) AND hangs `adb start-server`. The unconditional pre-poll form proposed on the strength of the 0.00 s warm measurement is therefore WITHDRAWN and explicitly rejected in alternativesConsidered: it would burn the full 15 s watchdog on EVERY poll against a wedged daemon — a second livelock introduced by the fix itself and five times worse than the 3 s one it replaces. FR-36 keeps a budgeted, escalating, conditional form instead, with every step carrying its own budget.

HONESTY CARRIED, not smoothed over: the wedged case was NOT deterministic — start-server hung in one run and returned 0.00 s in another against the same stopped daemon. Unlike the cold-start cost, which was 3.03 s on all three runs. That non-determinism is precisely why no step may rely on observed timing and every step carries its own budget. A SIGSTOP-ed daemon is also only an APPROXIMATION of a real wedge (a half-open socket, a USB-stack hang); the recovery ladder is deliberately not over-fitted to this simulation — it is 'try to start, then force a restart, then report', which is the generic shape, not a signature match on this one symptom.

CAVEAT CARRIED: the 0.00 s warm measurement is the SAME adb binary talking to its own daemon. A version mismatch (a second adb from a different SDK on the machine) makes `start-server` kill and restart the daemon instead of no-opping, which WOULD disturb a live session. That is a pre-existing environment hazard, not caused by this fix, but no error path here assumes the 0.00 s case: the healing step only ever runs after a timeout-classified failure, when discovery is idle (sessionDeviceId == null gates the poll loop through flatMapLatest at MirrorViewModel.kt:146-147, so no live capture session exists while discovery polls), and it is budgeted.
